name: NGC 1052-DF8 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 1052-DF8, a low surface brightness galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc1052df8-hubble
story: A faint, diffuse galaxy first found in Dragonfly telescope images of the NGC 1052 field, where Hubble was sent to measure how far away it is. Star-forming clumps are clearly visible in its soft glow.

claims.text: NGC 1052-DF8 is one of the very low surface brightness objects observed with HST/ACS in program 14644
It was found in Dragonfly images and is a new discovery
HST was used to measure distances to the galaxies
Star-forming clumps are clearly visible in NGC 1052-DF8
